be afraid verb

also frightened, afraid, fear, scared, terrified, what are you afraid of?, afraid that, dread, I am afraid that, I’m afraid that, scared to death

classical

Traupman 269
Traupman 314

timeō, timēre, timuī

verb, second conjugation

be afraid, fear

Other words

  • territus, territa, territum — frightened, scared

    adjective (participle of terreō) · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. terreō; Andresian p. 36; Traupman 374

    Made afraid by something: perterritus, terrified.

  • metuō, metuere, metuī, metūtum — to fear, be afraid

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 149, 152

    Lewis & Short: a fear that something will happen; often with nē and the subjunctive.

  • vereor nē (+ subjunctive) — I am afraid that

    also used · classical · Traupman 149

    After verbs of fearing nē means “that” and ut (or nē nōn) “that not”: vereor nē pluat, I’m afraid it will rain.

  • formīdō, formīdāre, formīdāvī, formīdātum — to dread

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 151

  • formīdulōsus, formīdulōsa, formīdulōsum — fearful; frightening

    also used · classical · Traupman 149; Ter. Eun. 757 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 269

    Lewis & Short: “full of fear”, both active (causing fear) and passive (afraid).

  • vereor, verērī, veritus sum — fear, be afraid; “I am afraid that” is vereor nē + subjunctive

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.12.3: vereor nē (Lewis & Short); Traupman 269

    After words of fearing nē means “that”, and ut or nē nōn “that not”: vereor nē veniat, I’m afraid he’ll come; vereor ut veniat, I’m afraid he won’t.

Examples

  • Quid timēs?

    What are you afraid of?composed

  • Timēsne? Vīsne dēscendere?

    Are you afraid? Do you want to climb down?composed

  • Quid est quod metuis?

    What are you afraid of?Traupman 92

  • exanimātus (-a) metū sum

    I am scared to deathTraupman 374

  • exanimāta metū

    frightened out of her witsTer. Ph. 3.3.32 (Lewis & Short s.v. exanimō)

See also happy, sad, scared to death, frighten.
